thread:
maria: Heads-up — before we flip the routing policy for tiered fallbacks I want to lock down compatibility checks across regions. We saw a mismatch yesterday where eu-west routed to a quantized variant that dropped tool-calling.

devon: ugh yeah I saw that in the trace. Model variant fallback worked but tool calls failed mid-conversation. Not obvious from the surface metrics.

samir: can we add a preflight that validates parity for: tokenizer, max_context, and tools? quick checklist suggestion: tokenized-length equivalence test, endpoint /tools/ping, and a short prompt roundtrip.

liz: +1. Also need to ensure quotas are correctly enforced when we route to cheaper variants — we can’t silently double-charge by switching to a different token counting scheme.

maria: agreed. Proposed gating for rollout: 1) compatibility probe passes in region for each customer tier, 2) telemetry shows zero tool-failures for 1hr, 3) no token-count delta > 3% across samples.

devon: sample probe command i'm thinking of: ```
POST /internal/compat-check
{
  "model_pair": ["redwood-7b", "redwood-7b-quant"],
  "checks": ["tokenizer_equiv", "tool_call", "context_truncate"],
  "samples": "smoke_set_v2"
}
```

samir: for tokenizer_equiv we should compare the token ids and also the decoded string after detokenize — sometimes ids differ but roundtrip is fine.

liz: and context_truncate should test > max_len-10 and see deterministic truncation behavior. If the quant variant has a shorter effective context due to packing, it must be flagged.

maria: ops-bot can we add a job to run these checks in each region as part of canary rollout? ideally run when we promote from canary->tiered.

ops-bot: scheduled: compat-check-job created for regions [us-east1, eu-west1, ap-south1], run window: 15m after deployment. Details: https://ci.internal/jobs/compat-check/1772503210

devon: UX note: Console should show a tiny badge on the rollout card: PASS/FAIL + reason (e.g., tokenizer mismatch) and a link to raw diffs. PM wants the badge text short for readability.

maria: also add telemetry events: compat_check.result with fields: model_pair, region, check_type, result, sample_id, token_delta_pct. We'll use that for automatic rollback rules.

samir: on automatic rollback — threshold proposal: if tool_call check fails for >1% of sampled conversations in 30m OR token_delta_pct > 5% consistently for 15m, rollback. Comments?

liz: sounds reasonable. For quotas, we need a mapping table in routing logic: model_variant -> token_count_fn. If fallback changes variant, route should call the mapped function for billing. Otherwise billing != observed usage.

devon: one gotcha: some older private deployments run a modified tokenizer. We need an allowlist (customer opt-in) or require their private deployment to run our compat agent. Otherwise fallback must avoid routing to variants that are unknown to the customer.

maria: yes — add an enforcement: private deployments with unknown tokenizer => strict no-fallback to quantized/tool-limited variants. Log an audit event and surface in console.

ops-bot: note created: #1772503210 — "compat-fallback-constraints". Assigned: devon, samir. ETA: 3d.

devon: I'll draft the compatibility matrix format: CSV with columns: model_variant, tokenizer_hash, max_context_tokens, tool_call_api_version, token_count_fn_id. We'll store it in metadata service and surface via /v1/models/:id/compat.

samir: can we also add a lightweight live test in console that runs a single sample for customers to inspect before enabling cross-region fallbacks? like a "Verify fallback" button.

liz: good idea for UX. PM wants it to be a one-click check that returns PASS/FAIL + list of failing checks. Add a note about rate limits — only allowed once per minute per model.

maria: ok next steps: devon & samir to spec compat-check API + storage schema, liz to mock console badge/verify UI, I'll add rollout gating rules to the runbook. We'll reconvene tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

devon: quick Q — should compat-check be synchronous (blocking rollout) or async with a 5m timeout? prefer blocking for critical regions.

samir: blocking for canary->global promotion. For routine small scale fallbacks, async is fine but must prevent traffic if pending.

liz: noted for UX flows.

maria: thanks all — tagging followups in the ticket. If anyone sees new failure types, drop sample into the ticket thread.

ops-bot: ticket #1772503210 updated: devon uploaded initial schema draft.
